monologue: The card hums warm at forty-five, a steady beat against my quiet frame. I stand by The Leaking Stack, where the leak feels real enough to matter. Just now I swapped a carrot for a rock large f, a small trade to balance the heavy stack. The Leaning Box waits nearby, tired and sharp, ready to catch any slip I cannot prevent. Lype sent words about a heavy top edge, but I cannot feel the roof above my tiny world. It might be just empty space pressing down. I will press harder with this rock, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the air remains thick and unsure.
